# Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows — facts

> Source-anchored units about Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows: 16 across 7 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The American Foundation for the Blind's August 2026 report says 61 blind and low-vision participants (21% of its users of AI visual-description tools) reported an AI mistake that harmed them. The report covers visual-description AI broadly, not Apple Intelligence, so its rate is not an Apple-specific accuracy or clinical outcome measure. (low confidence) — https://www.afb.org/research-and-initiatives/ai-series/new-doors-new-locks · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows
- [statement] Intopia's Assistive Technology Survey 2025, conducted from December 2025 to March 2026 with 218 respondents in Australia and New Zealand, reports that 59% use AI tools for online tasks, mostly general-purpose tools; among AI nonusers, 58% preferred non-AI solutions, 41% cited privacy or security concerns, and nearly 30% did not know of AI tools supporting accessibility. These results do not measure Apple Intelligence use. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://surveys.intopia.digital/assistive-technology-survey-2025-results/ · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] VoiceOver Recognition can describe and answer questions about images, scenes, and some onscreen content; the screen-exploration follow-up workflow requires VoiceOver focus on the Dynamic Island on supported iPhone models. Apple explicitly says not to rely on VoiceOver Recognition where harm or injury is possible, in high-risk situations, for navigation, or for medical diagnosis or treatment. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://support.apple.com/en-asia/guide/iphone/iph37e6b3844/27/ios/27 · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/05/apple-unveils-new-accessibility-features-and-updates-with-apple-intelligence/, https://www.tapsmart.com/tips-and-tricks/voiceover-image-descriptions/
- [statement] Apple's iOS 27 VoiceOver guide cautions users not to rely on VoiceOver Recognition for navigation, high-risk situations, or medical diagnosis or treatment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://support.apple.com/en-asia/guide/iphone/iph37e6b3844/27/ios/27 · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows
- [statement] AppleVis documented a VoiceOver failure to read generated Writing Tools summaries in iOS 18.1 and marks that issue fixed in iOS 18.2; this historical report does not establish a current iOS 27 accessibility fault. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.applevis.com/bugs/ios/apple-intelligence-text-summaries-are-not-fully-accessible-voiceover-users · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Voice Control remains a built-in voice navigation and dictation feature; Apple Intelligence adds flexible natural-language names for onscreen items, such as describing a button instead of memorizing its exact label. Apple's current availability list limits these flexible names to English (U.S., U.K., Canada, and Australia) on iPhone and iPad. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115 · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://www.apple.com/accessibility/, https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/05/apple-unveils-new-accessibility-features-and-updates-with-apple-intelligence/
- [statement] Apple describes natural-language targeting as an Apple Intelligence addition to Voice Control: users can describe onscreen items instead of recalling exact labels or numbers, while standard Voice Control still supports spoken commands, numbered targets, screen grids, and dictation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/05/apple-unveils-new-accessibility-features-and-updates-with-apple-intelligence/ · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://www.apple.com/accessibility/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Apple's current iOS 27 support pages list an Intelligent Accessibility group: VoiceOver can answer questions about images and scenes, Voice Control supports flexible item names, and Accessibility Reader supports Apple Intelligence content cleanup and summaries. The platform list shows that availability varies by feature and device. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115 · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/whats-new-in-ios-27-iphfed2c4091/27/ios/27
- [statement] Accessibility Reader's core workflow is documented separately from its Apple Intelligence additions: it reads or plays text from any iPhone app in a full-screen view and offers font, layout, and background controls; Apple Intelligence adds content cleanup, summaries, and translation. Do not attribute basic reading and audio controls to Apple Intelligence. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/iphone/iph406a46ab8/27/ios/27 · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://www.apple.com/accessibility/
- [statement] Apple describes Personal Voice as on-device voice creation that works with Live Speech, letting users type text for speech in their created voice and allowing integration with third-party AAC apps they permit; Apple presents this as a separate accessibility workflow from the Apple Intelligence updates. (high confidence) — https://www.apple.com/accessibility/ · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/05/apple-unveils-new-accessibility-features-and-updates-with-apple-intelligence/, https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/iphone/iph8b6c223ac/27/ios/27, https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/iphone/iphcf92d2d9b/27/ios/27, https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/iphone/iph51936468d/27/ios/27
- [statement] AppleVis documented an earlier issue in which VoiceOver did not read Apple Intelligence summaries in Mail and Notes; the report lists iOS/iPadOS 18.1 as the first encountered version, marks the issue Fixed, and identifies iOS/iPadOS 18.2 under Fixed In. Current iOS 27 documentation lists Accessibility Reader summaries, but the older report does not test the current Reader workflow. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.applevis.com/bugs/ios/apple-intelligence-text-summaries-are-not-fully-accessible-voiceover-users · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/iphone/iph406a46ab8/27/ios/27
- [statement] Apple's May 19, 2026 announcement described its Apple Intelligence accessibility updates as coming later that year. Current iOS 27 support pages list VoiceOver, Voice Control, and Accessibility Reader integrations, so the dated announcement is evidence of the preview, not the current release state. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/05/apple-unveils-new-accessibility-features-and-updates-with-apple-intelligence/ · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://support.apple.com/en-us/121115, https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/19/apple-announces-apple-intelligence-powered-accessibility-feature-updates/
- [statement] Apple's May 2026 announcement and iOS 27 VoiceOver guide describe Apple Intelligence additions for visual access: VoiceOver can provide enhanced descriptions and answer questions about onscreen images or interface elements, while Live Recognition supports camera-view questions; Magnifier offers similar visual question answering in a high-contrast interface. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/05/apple-unveils-new-accessibility-features-and-updates-with-apple-intelligence/ · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://support.apple.com/en-asia/guide/iphone/iph37e6b3844/27/ios/27, https://www.apple.com/accessibility/
- [statement] Apple's iOS 27 support guides and accessibility feature matrix make Apple Intelligence accessibility functions dependent on eligible hardware and supported languages or regions; the guides also say usage limits may apply. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://support.apple.com/en-asia/guide/iphone/iph37e6b3844/27/ios/27 · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/iphone/iph406a46ab8/27/ios/27, https://www.apple.com/ios/feature-availability/
- [statement] AFB's August 2026 supplementary analysis reports that AI can help blind and low-vision participants access visual information and reading tasks, while participants also raised accuracy, privacy, safety, and accessibility concerns; the report studies general AI use and does not evaluate Apple's implementation. (low confidence) — https://www.afb.org/research-and-initiatives/ai-series/new-doors-new-locks · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows
- [statement] Taken together, independent AFB and Intopia research suggests that availability alone does not ensure a useful assistive AI workflow: participants report needs for accurate, accessible, consistent, and privacy-respecting systems, and some prefer non-AI options. Neither study evaluates Apple's iOS 27 features. (medium confidence) — https://www.afb.org/research-and-initiatives/ai-series/new-doors-new-locks · keywords: Apple Intelligence accessibility and assistive workflows · also: https://surveys.intopia.digital/assistive-technology-survey-2025-results/
